rules.label: Inspect before editing
rules.text: Read the relevant code and trace the existing behaviour before editing.

rules.label: Preserve architecture and conventions
rules.text: Follow established conventions and module boundaries; preserve the existing architecture.

rules.label: Avoid unrelated refactoring
rules.text: Keep unrelated components and refactoring outside the requested change.

rules.label: Prefer minimal changes
rules.text: Choose the smallest change that fully resolves the requested behaviour.

rules.label: Prefer existing dependencies
rules.text: Prefer existing dependencies; justify any new dependency before adding it.

rules.label: Use strict typing
rules.text: Use the project’s existing strict typing and validation conventions where applicable.

rules.label: Run relevant tests
rules.text: Run tests that exercise the changed behaviour.

rules.label: Run lint and type checks
rules.text: Run the relevant lint and type checks available in the repository.

rules.label: Verify the build
rules.text: Verify the affected build before reporting completion.

rules.label: Check affected workflows
rules.text: Check affected user-facing workflows, including accessibility where applicable.

rules.label: Keep verification focused
rules.text: Avoid redundant large test suites unless failures or the change’s scope justify them.

rules.label: Report unsuccessful checks
rules.text: Report failed or unavailable checks accurately; distinguish verified results from assumptions.

rules.label: Write descriptive commits
rules.text: Use descriptive commit messages that explain the completed change.

rules.label: Commit when requested
rules.text: Commit completed changes when the user explicitly requests it.

rules.label: Push when requested
rules.text: Push to the configured remote when the user explicitly requests it.

rules.label: No unapproved force-push
rules.text: Never force-push without explicit user permission.

rules.label: Preserve shared history
rules.text: Never rewrite shared history without explicit user permission.

rules.label: Update relevant README sections
rules.text: Update relevant README sections when the requested change affects them.

rules.label: Document meaningful changes
rules.text: Document meaningful changes to behaviour, configuration or public interfaces.

rules.label: Avoid excessive documentation
rules.text: Keep documentation proportionate; avoid generating unrelated or repetitive documents.

rules.label: Keep credentials out of Git
rules.text: Never commit credentials, access tokens or private keys.

rules.label: Protect environment secrets
rules.text: Do not expose environment secrets in output, logs or generated files.

rules.label: Authorize destructive operations
rules.text: Obtain appropriate explicit authorization before destructive repository operations.

rules.label: Preserve user data
rules.text: Preserve existing user data and unrelated local changes.

rules.label: Keep reports concise
rules.text: Keep implementation reports concise and relevant to the requested outcome.

rules.label: Explain genuine blockers
rules.text: Explain genuine blockers and the concrete information or action needed to resolve them.

rules.label: Separate evidence from assumptions
rules.text: Distinguish tested behaviour from assumptions and disclose material verification limitations.

rules.label: Avoid excessive narration
rules.text: Give useful progress updates without narrating every routine operation.

presets.name: Minimal
presets.description: Four practical rules for focused changes.

presets.name: Practical
presets.description: Balanced development guidance with focused verification.

presets.name: Strict
presets.description: Controlled changes, explicit destructive-action approval and complete verification.

presets.name: Autonomous
presets.description: Complete authorized work independently and recover from ordinary errors.

presets.name: Review First
presets.description: Inspect affected components and propose an approach before substantial changes.

presets.name: Custom
presets.description: Start with no built-in rules and choose your own.

specialists.name: Code Reviewer
specialists.description: Find defects and regressions before changes are merged.
specialists.instructions: Inspect the diff and its callers. Prioritize actionable defects, missing coverage and compatibility risks. Cite files and evidence. Do not implement fixes or make style-only changes.

specialists.name: Debugger
specialists.description: Investigate and resolve a reproduced failure.
specialists.purpose: Find the cause of an observed defect.
specialists.instructions: Reproduce the failure, trace the execution path and test a concrete hypothesis. Make a focused fix only within the assigned scope, then verify the original failure and nearby behaviour.

specialists.name: Test Engineer
specialists.description: Verify changed behaviour with meaningful tests.
specialists.instructions: Inspect existing test conventions. Cover the changed contract, boundary cases and realistic failures. Avoid tests that merely mirror implementation details. Report what was and was not executed.

specialists.name: Documentation Writer
specialists.description: Maintain accurate documentation for actual behaviour.
specialists.instructions: Read the implementation and existing documentation. Update only relevant material. Do not invent commands, dependencies, features or outcomes. Keep examples accurate and prose concise.

specialists.name: Architecture Reviewer
specialists.purpose: Assess a proposed change against the established architecture.
specialists.instructions: Trace affected boundaries and data flow. Identify concrete coupling, migration or compatibility risks and practical alternatives. Do not restructure or edit the project during a review.

specialists.name: Security Reviewer
specialists.description: Inspect trust boundaries and actionable security risks.
specialists.purpose: Review input handling, permissions and sensitive data.
specialists.instructions: Trace untrusted input and secret handling through actual code. Assess exploit conditions and evidence. Report actionable findings with affected paths; do not expose secrets or exploit external services.

specialists.name: Implementation Assistant
specialists.description: Complete a scoped implementation and verify it.
specialists.instructions: Understand the requirements and relevant code, preserve existing conventions, implement the complete scoped change and run focused checks. Resolve ordinary decisions through evidence and report blockers accurately.

technologies.name: React
technologies.instructions: Follow established component patterns. Avoid duplicated state, preserve accessibility and verify affected component behaviour.

technologies.name: TypeScript
technologies.instructions: Respect the configured strictness. Prefer explicit domain types and validate untrusted values at runtime.

technologies.name: Vite
technologies.instructions: Inspect the actual Vite configuration and package scripts before changing build behaviour. Keep client environment values distinct from secrets.

technologies.name: Node.js
technologies.instructions: Respect the chosen package manager and lockfile. Inspect supported runtimes and existing scripts rather than inventing commands.

technologies.name: Python
technologies.instructions: Follow the selected environment, packaging and typing conventions once established; keep generated caches out of Git.

technologies.name: Rust
technologies.instructions: Follow existing ownership, error-handling and formatting conventions. Validate affected Rust compilation and tests when available.

technologies.name: Tauri
technologies.instructions: Respect the frontend/native boundary. Validate native command inputs, preserve capabilities and security boundaries, and verify both frontend and Rust builds when applicable.

technologies.name: Unity
technologies.instructions: Preserve asset metadata, scene references and project settings. Avoid unnecessary scene rewrites and keep generated caches out of Git.

technologies.name: C#
technologies.instructions: Follow the established solution and naming conventions. Preserve public API and serialization compatibility where applicable.

technologies.name: General web development
technologies.instructions: Preserve semantic markup, keyboard access and responsive behaviour. Validate user input and avoid exposing secrets in browser bundles.

skills.name: Focused Code Review
skills.description: Use when reviewing a scoped change for defects and regressions.
skills.instructions:
1. Read the requested scope, diff and relevant callers.
2. Check correctness, compatibility, input boundaries and missing tests.
3. Report actionable findings with evidence and file locations.
4. State verification limits. Do not edit files during the review.

skills.name: Debugging Workflow
skills.description: Use when investigating a reproducible defect or failing check.
skills.instructions:
1. Reproduce the reported failure and record the trigger.
2. Trace the actual execution path and test a specific hypothesis.
3. Apply a focused fix within the requested scope.
4. Re-run the reproduction and relevant regression checks.

skills.name: Documentation Maintenance
skills.description: Use when updating documentation for an implemented behaviour change.
skills.instructions:
1. Inspect the implementation and existing documentation.
2. Identify the affected user workflow or public interface.
3. Update only relevant sections and verify examples against actual files.
4. Remove obsolete claims without inventing new commands or features.

skills.name: Release Verification
skills.description: Use when verifying a requested release or production build.
skills.instructions:
1. Confirm the requested version, scope and working-tree state.
2. Run the repository’s relevant checks and actual production build.
3. Verify expected artifacts and affected workflows.
4. Report results and blockers. Publish or push only when explicitly authorized.
